shared_elements: upright carved stone slab/monolith displayed in a museum
low-relief carving on the principal face
circular/disc motifs (round shields in A, concentric discs in B)
horizontal division of the surface into stacked zones or bands
justification: Both are tall, upright relief-carved stones whose ornament is organised into stacked horizontal zones, and both include prominent round disc forms (shields in A, concentric circles in B). But A is a crisply cut, pale, narrative relief with legible warriors, a horse and a framing zigzag border, whereas B is a dark, heavily weathered block with shallow, abstract, schematic motifs and no discernible scene, so the resemblance is generic rather than compositional.
